title: Choose the Pipeline Debugger composition
question: Which composition should govern the site? The hybrid keeps one visual system while letting each task lead with its strongest surface.

options.label: Task-led hybrid
options.thesis: Trace-first teaches the lifecycle, notebook-first decodes the photos, and ledger-first audits model transparency.
options.viewport: The landing page uses the trace-first composition; notebook and report pages inherit the same controls and probes with task-specific density.
options.risk: Shared component grammar must be strict so the topology changes feel intentional rather than like separate products.

options.label: Trace everywhere
options.thesis: Every page single-steps left-to-right through one dominant execution trace.
options.viewport: Lifecycle rail, dominant token-to-release trace, proof inspector, and lab console.
options.risk: The notebook photos and report matrix have to fight the trace for space.

options.label: Notebook everywhere
options.lineage: source workbench and live proof inspector
options.thesis: The learner always begins from one photographed question and translates it into math and code.
options.viewport: Large notebook source, normalized concept, and live systems inspector.
options.risk: It underplays the full lifecycle and makes later systems topics feel secondary.

options.label: Ledger everywhere
options.thesis: Every lesson begins from a missing disclosure or experiment artifact in the transparent-report matrix.
options.viewport: Release ledger, selected scaling experiment, transparency inspector, and token-to-release trace.
options.risk: It is powerful for synthesis but too advanced as the first contact with Transformer fundamentals.
